html: If there’s one place in Sri Lanka where you can get up close and personal with the country’s most beloved animal, it’s the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage. Set along the banks of the Maha Oya River, this sanctuary offers a heartwarming experience where visitors can witness elephants being cared for, fed, and even bathing playfully in the river. For travelers with Tours 999, a day at Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage Sri Lanka promises an unforgettable blend of wildlife, education, and compassion — all within a beautiful natural setting.

The Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage was established in 1975 by the Sri Lanka Department of Wildlife Conservation to provide refuge to orphaned, abandoned, or injured elephants found in the wild. What began with just a few elephants has now grown into one of the world’s most recognized elephant care facilities, housing over 80 majestic elephants.

Unlike traditional zoos, the Pinnawala Orphanage functions as both a sanctuary and a research center — dedicated to the welfare, breeding, and rehabilitation of Asian elephants. Its success stories include several generations of elephants being born and raised under careful supervision, symbolizing hope for the species’ survival.

text: The Experience: What to See and Do

html: A visit to Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage Sri Lanka is more than just sightseeing; it’s a full sensory experience that captures the bond between humans and elephants. Here’s what awaits you during your visit:
1. Bottle-Feeding Baby Elephants

One of the most heartwarming moments you’ll witness at Pinnawala is the bottle-feeding session. Every morning and afternoon, caretakers feed the baby elephants large bottles of milk, often with the help of visitors. Watching these playful calves eagerly drink their milk is a joyful and emotional experience — one that delights both children and adults alike.
If you’re traveling with Tours 999, your guide will help you time your visit perfectly to witness this special moment.
2. River Bathing – A Mesmerizing Sight

After feeding time, the elephants are led in groups down a small road to the Maha Oya River, where they spend hours bathing and socializing. This daily ritual, which takes place twice a day, is the highlight of any visit.

Imagine the sight — dozens of elephants splashing, playing, and cooling off in the water while tourists watch from the riverbank or nearby cafes. The sound of their trumpeting and the sheer joy in their movements make this one of the most photographed moments in Sri Lanka.
From a shaded spot, you can capture beautiful photos or simply sit back and enjoy the serene, almost spiritual atmosphere.
3. Feeding and Observation

In addition to milk feeding, visitors can help feed adult elephants fruits like bananas and jackfruit. This close interaction offers a chance to feel their rough trunks and understand their gentle nature up close.
Tours 999 guides ensure guests enjoy these experiences responsibly — without disturbing or stressing the animals.

Pinnawala isn’t just about entertainment; it’s also a place of education and conservation. Informational displays around the site explain elephant behavior, biology, and the threats they face in the wild.

Many visitors are surprised to learn that Sri Lanka’s elephant population has significantly declined due to habitat loss and human-wildlife conflict. The orphanage plays a crucial role in raising awareness and demonstrating how humans can coexist with these magnificent creatures.

As with many wildlife attractions, ethical tourism is an important topic at Pinnawala. Over the years, some travelers have raised concerns about elephant welfare, especially regarding captivity and interaction-based tourism.
At Tours 999, we believe in responsible travel — experiences that are both enjoyable and ethical. When visiting Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage Sri Lanka, travelers are encouraged to:

• Observe elephants from a respectful distance
  • Avoid any activities that involve riding or unnatural performances
  • Support conservation efforts by purchasing tickets directly from official counters
  • Follow guide instructions and avoid feeding elephants unsupervised
By practicing mindful tourism, visitors contribute to the orphanage’s ongoing mission of protecting Sri Lanka’s elephants.
• Location: Pinnawala is located about 90 kilometers from Colombo and 40 kilometers from Kandy, making it a convenient stop on your route through Sri Lanka’s cultural triangle.
• Opening Hours: The orphanage is open daily from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM. The best times to visit are during the feeding and bathing sessions, which usually occur around 9:15 AM, 1:15 PM, and 2:15 PM.
• Entrance Fees: Ticket prices vary for locals and foreigners. Your Tours 999 guide will handle ticketing and timing to ensure you get the best experience.
• Photography Tips: Bring a camera with a good zoom lens to capture the river bathing from a comfortable distance. Early morning offers the best light for photography.

  • Royal Botanical Gardens, Peradeniya – A lush escape filled with orchids and tropical plants.
